title: Synchronize Company OKRs into Rolling Initiative Map and Cross-Org Dependency Registry
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Create a single source of truth that maps company-level OKRs to active initiatives across Product, Engineering, Design and GTM, surface cross-org dependencies, and provide a lightweight operational cadence for weekly updates and escalation. Scope: design the initiative mapping template, build a dependency registry schema, migrate current initiative owners into the map, and deliver a first-pass integration with the Roadmap dashboard and rollout calendar. Out of scope: full automation of sync with individual team tools (we will surface CSV/Google Sheet import for v1).
acceptance_criteria: A standardized initiative record format (OKR-linked, owner, milestone dates, dependency list, risk & mitigation) is approved by PM and Eng leads

A populated initiative map covering 100% of company-level OKR-aligned initiatives (all initiatives with >$50k runway or >1 squad) is available in the shared Drive and linked from the Roadmap dashboard
A dependency registry with searchable fields (dependent team, dependency type, SLA impact, resolution owner) is accessible and populated for at least 80% of initiatives
Weekly operational cadence defined: owners commit to a 1-line weekly update that appears in the initiative map and triggers alerts for 'blocked' state
Integration wireframe for Roadmap dashboard that surfaces OKR alignment, key milestones, and highest-severity dependencies is reviewed and approved by Design and PM
decisions: Adopt a lightweight initiative record rather than heavy PRD to encourage adoption (one page template + metadata fields)
Use Google Drive + a canonical CSV export/import for v1 of the registry to minimize engineering build time
Prioritize dependencies that can cause availability/cost/regulatory impact as high-severity and surface them in the dashboard first
Roll out ownership and weekly cadence through leadership reviews rather than mandatory tooling enforcement for the first quarter
tradeoffs: Speed vs. completeness: CSV + Drive allows rapid rollout but will require manual curation and owner discipline
Tooling vs. adoption: delaying an integrated product feature reduces developer workload now but risks inconsistent updates across teams
Granularity vs. noise: capturing every micro-dependency will create noise; we will bias to dependencies with cross-org impact or SLA risk
updates_history: 2026-02-22: Kickoff with PM, Eng, Design leads. Agreed on scope and v1 constraints. Action: Draft initiative template assigned to DES-319.
2026-02-27: Template iteration reviewed. Design suggested reducing required fields to improve completion rates. PM accepted suggestions.
2026-03-03: Engineering input: proposed schema for dependency categorization (availability, cost, schedule, compliance). ENG-4021 flagged as potential dependent initiative.
2026-03-05: Leadership sync: Requested that priorities map back to Q1 company OKRs and that legal review any dependencies marked 'regulatory' before publication.
2026-03-08: First pass population: 22 initiatives added to Drive map by initiative owners; 16 dependency lines recorded. Observability: need a simple filter for high-severity dependencies.
2026-03-10: Design sign-off on Roadmap dashboard wireframe. Next step: implement CSV import and display prototype in Product weekly review (2026-03-15).

risks_mitigation: Risk: Owners don't keep the map up to date. Mitigation: Keep required update a single-line weekly ask tied to performance review signals for Q2 trial.
Risk: Manual CSV processes cause stale data. Mitigation: Build simple validation on import to flag missing owner or due date fields.
Risk: Over-indexing on low-impact dependencies. Mitigation: Use a 3-point severity rubric and only auto-surface severity >= 2 in dashboard alerts.
